- Overestimate prices in the short term after sentiment spikes (especially >0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (<0.4) — add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag 1–2 days behind true price movements — adjust forward by 0.5–1.5% for the next 3–5 days.
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high if sentiment >0.7.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to noise.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid over-relying on recent 7–14 day trends — weight older data more heavily if sentiment is stable.
